Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Australia's reply. The Indians disperse from the huddle and spread out on the field. The Aussie skipper, Alyssa Healy, walks out to open alongside Phoebe Litchfield. Renuka Singh Thakur will have the first crack with the new ball. Healy is on strike. A slip in place. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Surface with something for everyone - As they say, if it seams, it spins, and that has certainly been the case today at Allan Border Field. Even as the ball got older, it continued to do a bit off the seam, and Alana King, with her control, managed to extract handy purchase from the surface. The extra bounce is something Australia will have to contend with in their chase. They would be better served looking to play down the ground, as several of the Indian dismissals came from batters playing square of the wicket. All the ingredients of an intriguing chase are in place. Stick around.

A brief revival, but Australia close the door - India did find some stability through a vital 53-run stand between Harmanpreet Kaur and Kashvee Gautam that briefly raised hopes of pushing towards 250, but Australia struck again by dismissing Kaur at a crucial juncture. That left Kashvee Gautam battling with the tail. She did not quite get the desired support, and in hindsight, Gautam could have managed the situation better by farming the strike more effectively. If not for the dropped catch by Tahlia McGrath when Gautam was on 17, Australia might have managed to keep India under 200.

From edges to elegance - Smriti Mandhana began in scratchy fashion, with a few edgy boundaries that could so easily have gone to hand, but she survived that testing phase. Mandhana grew in confidence and got a partnership going with Harmanpreet Kaur, but the hosts were able to nip the threat of the stand in the bud at just the right time. They were able to apply the squeeze from there and pick up a couple of wickets along the way to reduce India to 140/6.

Early blows rocked India - Despite there being a bit of cloud cover, Harmanpreet Kaur opted to bat first. India were rocked early by the Aussie new ball attack, who made full use of the swing and seam on offer to ask all the right questions of the top order. Jemimah Rodrigues could not do much either.

A disciplined and well-rounded bowling effort - A job well done from Australia. They never allowed India to get on top, and whenever the visitors threatened to build momentum, the hosts struck back and wrested control of the proceedings.

The ODI leg begins with high stakes - A 4-2 lead, a fresh format, and a farewell storyline, the stakes could not be better poised as Australia Women take on India in the 1st ODI of this three-match series at Allan Border Field. With two points awarded for each white-ball win and four reserved for the one-off Test, Australia Women know this ODI leg is their chance to swing the momentum after India clinched the T20Is 2-1. Adding emotion to the contest, this series marks the final international appearances in Australian colours for Alyssa Healy, who missed the T20Is but returns in a format where she averages 42.05 against India and will be eager to make an impact. Australia Women's fortress record - Australia Wome's home dominance in WODIs is formidable, just two defeats in their last 21 matches in these conditions. Beth Mooney and Phoebe Litchfield have been standout performers over the past year, combining for over 800 runs, while Ellyse Perry continues to set benchmarks, recently becoming the first Australian woman to earn 350 international caps.
